choices: Store-and-forward verifies the FCS before forwarding, adding one frame time of latency but never propagating corruption
Cut-through cannot be used above 1 Gb/s
explanation: Cut-through forwards after reading the destination address, giving sub-microsecond latency, and will happily forward a frame that turns out to be corrupt. The choice is a latency-against-error-propagation trade, and low-latency trading fabrics make it differently from enterprise access switches.
